background.source: An amphiphile is a chemical compound that possesses both hydrophilic and lipophilic properties, meaning it has a love for both water and fat. These compounds have become the basis for various research areas in the fields of chemistry and biochemistry. For example, phospholipid amphiphiles, which are major structural components within cell membranes, are of particular interest. Additionally, common amphiphilic compounds such as surfactants can be found in everyday household products such as soaps, detergents, and lipoproteins. Organic compounds that contain hydrophilic groups at both ends of the molecule, known as bolaamphiphilic, can form prolate micelles when aggregated.
background.target: A neutral country is a state that takes a non-combatant approach towards belligerents in specific wars or permanently remains neutral in all future conflicts. Such countries avoid entering into military alliances to deter aggression using a sizeable military. Some neutral countries, like Austria and Ireland, have active UN peacekeeping forces and are part of political alliances such as the European Union. However, different nations interpret their neutrality differently, with some demilitarizing, like Costa Rica, and others holding to "armed neutrality" like Switzerland. In recent years, there has been a shift in how neutral conduct is perceived, with some countries, such as Sweden, abandoning its policy in the wake of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. This shift has mostly been due to the influence of pro-American and pro-Russian factions. Despite changes, nationals of neutral countries enjoy protection under the law of war, making them better protected from belligerent actions than other non-combatants.
